title: Find the Maximum Events in a Time Window
real_world_story: A real-time monitoring system receives events continuously and needs to determine the highest number of events recorded within any fixed time window.

real_world_connection.system: Real-time event and log monitoring system
real_world_connection.input_represents: The number of events received during consecutive time intervals
real_world_connection.target_represents: The maximum number of events occurring within a fixed-size monitoring window
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Moving a fixed-size window across event data while efficiently maintaining the current event count

problem_statement: Given an array representing the number of events received during consecutive time intervals and an integer K, find the maximum total number of events recorded in any K consecutive intervals.
task: Analyze the event stream using a fixed-size sliding window and return the maximum number of events observed in any K consecutive intervals.
input_format: The first line contains an integer N, the number of time intervals. The second line contains N space-separated integers representing the number of events in each interval. The third line contains an integer K, the size of the monitoring window.
output_format: Print a single integer representing the maximum number of events present in any K consecutive intervals.

examples.explanation: The window [5, 1, 8] contains 14 events, which is the maximum total.
The window [7, 3] contains the maximum total of 10 events.

expected_algorithm.name: Sliding Window
expected_algorithm.reason: A fixed-size monitoring window can be moved across the event stream while adding the new interval and removing the interval that leaves the window.

hint: Calculate the total number of events in the first K intervals.
Move the window one position at a time.
Add the new interval and subtract the interval that leaves the window.
real_world_takeaway: Sliding Window allows monitoring systems to analyze large event streams efficiently without repeatedly calculating the total for every time window.
